At first Ukrainian boats to Krynky carried 8–10 people; after losses, three-person boats took over.
There was "hardly any" electronic warfare on the Ukrainian boats, only a large EW system protecting the landing points.
The Prytula Foundation bought eight hexacopters (20 kg payload) and 40 "Mamont" 10-inch FPV carriers for the Krynky brigades; each of the four brigades got two hexacopters and ten Mamonts.
Ukrainian cargo drones carried ammunition, food, water and even blood to Krynky.
Ukrainian artillery and HIMARS fired from the right bank in support of Krynky.
Yurii Sodol promised that "HIMARS will fire like machine guns"; a 36th Marine Brigade source says the promise was not kept.

cites.quote: HIMARS will fire like machine guns

text: The Russian forces at Krynky belonged to the "Dnepr" Grouping of Forces.
Col Gen Oleg Makarevich was reportedly replaced as Dnepr grouping commander in late October 2023 by Col Gen Mikhail Teplinsky, the VDV commander.
Russian milbloggers called for Teplinsky's resignation after the 104th Division's December 2023 failure at Krynky.
Maj Gen Vladimir Zavadsky, deputy commander of the Russian 14th Army Corps, was killed near Krynky on 28 November 2023.
Elements of the Russian 49th Combined Arms Army, including the 205th Motor Rifle Regiment, had been on the Dnipro east bank since November 2022.
The new Russian 18th Combined Arms Army, with the 22nd Army Corps and the 70th Motor Rifle Division (26th MRR), was the main responder at Krynky in October–November 2023, and under-strength.
The Russian 177th Naval Infantry Regiment (Caspian Flotilla) was at Krynky in November 2023.
The Russian 810th Naval Infantry Brigade (Black Sea Fleet) was redeployed to the Krynky sector in October 2023.
The Russian 810th Naval Infantry Brigade made failed assaults at Krynky in November 2023.
Shoigu praised the 810th Naval Infantry Brigade in February 2024.
The Russian 7th Guards Air Assault (Mountain) Division, including the 171st Battalion / 97th Regiment, was at the Antonivskyi bridge in June 2023, with elements near Pishchanivka in November 2023.
The Russian 144th Motor Rifle Brigade and 28th Motor Rifle Regiment counterattacked at Krynky in late November 2023.
A column of the Russian 35th Separate Motor Rifle Brigade was hit at Hladkivka on 10 November 2023.
The new Russian 104th Guards Air Assault Division made its combat debut at Krynky in early December 2023 with heavy losses.
The Russian 81st Volunteer Spetsnaz Brigade was near Krynky in February 2024.
The Russian 80th Arctic Brigade (14th Army Corps) was on the Kherson direction in July 2024.
Kevliuk says the Russian Dnepr grouping grew from about 64,000 in November 2023 to about 100,000, "with some estimates of even 120,000", by July 2024.
In autumn 2023 Russia had thinned the Dnipro left-bank sector to reinforce Zaporizhzhia and treated it as quiet.
Russian Su-34s dropped glide bombs on Krynky from about 50 km away, beyond Ukrainian air defence in the sector.
The UMPK kit gives FAB bombs a range of 30–90 km, typically 60–70 km.
Russian glide bombs flattened much of Krynky from winter 2023–24.
Russian glide bombs hit Ukrainian marine positions at Krynky "with near-impunity for months".
A Ukrainian reconnaissance soldier called KABs "the least scary because you understand that they will hit, and you won't feel anything".

cites.quote: the least scary because you understand that they will hit, and you won't feel anything

text: Russian drones over the Dnipro crossings "are always on the hunt", boat motors are loud, and spotted boats draw FPVs or mortars.
By March 2024 Russia launched up to 80 FPVs a day at Krynky, including a new winged long-range FPV.
notes: the 80/day figure is attributed to Brovdi in the timeline row

text: From late winter 2024, Russian fire at the river mouths and landing points meant Ukrainian boats were hit on approach or on exit.
It "usually takes a few minutes" for a Ukrainian landing near Krynky to be passed to Russian mortar crews.
The landing points were among the deadliest places in the Krynky operation.
Russian Iskander missiles hit Ukrainian troops massed at the Antonivka rail bridge.
Russia used the TOS-1A thermobaric launcher at close range at Krynky.
Russian drones dropped anti-tank mines on Ukrainian positions at Krynky.
In summer 2024 Russian drones dropped incendiaries on Ukrainian positions near Krynky.
Ukrainian marines at Krynky reported Russian gas attacks.
notes: testimony only; no OPCW finding sourced

text: The Kyiv Independent reports "prohibited chemical weapons" among Russian tactics at Krynky.
In February 2024 Humeniuk described Russian "human wave" assaults without armour at Krynky.
A Ukrainian platoon commander said Russia attacked at Krynky seven to eight times a day, with groups that shrank from 6–7 men to 3–4, including VDV and Spetsnaz.

text: Lykhovii said that by late July 2024 Russia made 2–4 assaults a day near Krynky, sometimes a dozen.
Russian forces at Krynky did not mass at the very front, defending in depth.
Russian forces had "elaborate dugouts" and mines, and an "exceptionally fortified" line east of Krynky.
Ukrainian marines drilled small-boat disembarkation for Krynky; the 501st recce dropped life jackets because taking one off on shore costs about 30 seconds.

text: "Camels", or "logisticians", waited at the Krynky shore to guide new Ukrainian arrivals.
Ukrainian soldiers at Krynky kept apart so that "at least one of them survives to call in an evacuation".

text: The UK MoD noted "particularly effective use of small attack uncrewed aerial vehicles" by Ukraine at Krynky.

text: Brovdi claims 2,900 Russian drones downed or jammed at Krynky since October 2023 and about 77% of incoming drones defeated; some were hijacked and flown back.
Ukrainian HIMARS struck the Russian 35th Motor Rifle Brigade column at Hladkivka.
A Ukrainian regimental commander said Russian long-range artillery near Krynky was "heavily suppressed" by December 2023.
Ukraine resupplied the left bank at Krynky by drone, using hexacopters and Mamonts.
The Ukrainian Krynky operation lacked air defence against glide-bomb carriers, enough boats, EW on the boats, long-range fires and armour.
The US aid delay of early 2024 "likely only aggravated the problem" at Krynky.

text: From December 2023 Ukrainian night crossings to Krynky used inflatables and three-man boats on a 40–50 minute route through channels and islands, with loud motors and Russian drones overhead.
On the crossing to Krynky boats had to slow at the bends, the most dangerous points, and landed where Russian mortar fire followed within minutes.
Around 19 October 2023 the 36th Marine Brigade asked for a chain of 10–15 supply posts along the 3.5 km rail embankment, which had swamp on both sides, but was told to keep pushing to Poima.
Iskanders, air strikes and tank fire on the rail-bridge embankment around 19 October 2023 cost the 36th Marine Brigade 90 killed or wounded.
In the first Ukrainian landing in Krynky on 27 October 2023, thirteen men left a three-man boat and sank waist-deep in silt, with no guide; one marine shouted to the next crews to follow his voice.
After the 27 October 2023 landing the marines took over abandoned Russian trenches and fought street by street toward Kozachi Laheri.
Ukrainian marines held the forest on both flanks of Krynky for up to two months, under branches in the cold; the forest floor was strewn with Russian dead.
On 11 December 2023 a wounded marine's evacuation boat was hit; he swam one-armed to an island and paced the shore, soaking wet, from midnight to 06:00 so as not to freeze.
On 20–21 February 2024 a clip showed two Russian soldiers raising a flag at the edge of Krynky and then hurrying back, after Shoigu reported Krynky cleared.
Ukraine's Southern Command said Shoigu's report that Krynky was cleared was "not true".
By March 2024, 60–100 Ukrainian marines lived underground in Krynky's cellars through the daylight drone hours and came out at night to meet the boats.
When no boat could get through to Krynky, drones dropped life vests to the last Ukrainian men, who swam back.

counter: living underground in cellars by day
measure: Russian daylight drone hunting over Krynky
rationale: Marines lived underground through the daylight drone hours and came out only at night to meet the boats
effect: survival under daylight drone saturation; activity shifted to night

text: Ukrainian officers say the left-bank marine landing was planned for summer 2023 and postponed after the Kakhovka dam was destroyed; the Marine Corps went to Velyka Novosilka instead.

Ukrainska Pravda reads the June 2023 decision to send the marines to Velyka Novosilka as a way to "break in" the new brigades on land; allies had asked why the marines did not exploit the washed-out first line.
The maximum objective of the Krynky operation was Perekop, about 80 km away; the minimum was the left-bank line and the M-14, according to sources in the 36th Brigade and the Rada defence committee.
The Krynky plan gave three Ukrainian brigades on foot 3–4 days for a 30 km strip, with no second echelon.
A Ukrainian brigade commander says he "wouldn't have undertaken this operation" and that it "came from political leadership".
Ukrainian higher command never passed the marines' spring 2023 equipment list on to partners.
In late October to early November 2023, unable to hold three footholds, the Katran group gave up the rail-bridge and solar-farm footholds and reinforced Krynky.
In November 2023 Yermak announced the left-bank foothold in Washington, then the Marine Corps and General Staff declared bridgeheads, while Humeniuk urged "informational silence".

text: Michael Kofman said the Krynky operation "appears to have political objectives".
Kastehelmi said the Krynky operation became "more politically motivated" by winter 2023–24.
The Ukrainian General Staff's stated aim for the left-bank bridgeheads was to push Russian guns out of range of the west bank.

text: In October–December 2023 Teplinsky reportedly replaced Makarevich, and Russia committed the 104th VDV Division at Krynky.
Russia chose massed fires and attrition at Krynky rather than early mechanised counterattacks.
Ukrainian commanders never tried to bridge the Dnipro at Krynky; analysts say Russian bombers would have destroyed any attempt.
The Ukrainian withdrawal from Krynky was gradual: the 36th Marine Brigade went first, in winter, and the 35th last, in July 2024.
Most Ukrainska Pravda sources think the Krynky operation ran "at least several months longer than it should have".

text: One Ukrainian officer said: "We had to withdraw in spring at the latest, during the foggy season".

cites.quote: a fair question to ask if the operation should have been ended faster

text: A 35th Marine Brigade company commander defends holding the Krynky bridgehead as preventing Russian landings on the right bank.
The Ukrainian General Staff did not officially confirm the withdrawal from Krynky in July 2024.

text: Families of missing Krynky marines say their brigades stonewalled them.
One Ukrainska Pravda interviewee took part in interrogations in a criminal case against his commander for disobeying an order during the Krynky operation.
From 18 October 2023 one prominent Russian milblogger led alarmed reporting of an "offensive across the Dnipro" and accused the Russian MoD of ignoring the threat.
Russian milbloggers blamed Makarevich for the repeated Ukrainian landings on the left bank.
On 18 October 2023 Putin called the Ukrainian Dnipro activity the "next counteroffensive" and a failure.
In December 2023 Putin framed the Russian defence at Krynky as luring Ukrainians in to attrit them.
In December 2023 Putin said Russian troops had pulled back "several meters" near Krynky.
Kherson occupation head Saldo denied the August 2023 Kozachi Laheri landing, likely to avoid panic, in ISW's view.
Russian sources reported poor coordination, too few drones, weak artillery support and unevacuated wounded in the 810th Naval Infantry Brigade at Krynky.
The Ukrainian General Staff claimed desertions from the Russian 144th Motor Rifle Brigade at Krynky.

text: In February 2024 Shoigu claimed that Krynky was cleared and up to 3,500 Ukrainians killed, and called it the end of the 2023 counteroffensive.
ISW judged Shoigu's February 2024 claim that Krynky was cleared premature and timed for the March presidential election.
Russian milbloggers accused Shoigu of lying to Putin about Krynky.
A Kremlin claim in March 2024 that the whole Dnipro left bank was cleared angered Russian milbloggers, who called it fake.
On 17 July 2024 Russian sources claimed the Ukrainian withdrawal from Krynky before Ukraine acknowledged it.
On 17 July 2024 Russian sources reported small-arms fighting on the Dnipro delta islands.
